Messages.Author: TheLich
Messages.Body:
Name: J. Williford II
Cardtype: Ally
Unique Mortal Ally
1 Life 0 Bleed 0 Strength
You must control an investment in order to play J. Williford II
J. WIlliford II can move 1 blood from an investment you control to your pool or from the blood bank to an investment as a +1 Stealth Action.

Part of a series of cards which try to make investment cards a valid mechanic.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> TheLich wrote:
> Name: J. Williford II
> Cardtype: Ally
> Cost: 1 Pool
> Unique Mortal Ally
> 1 Life 0 Bleed 0 Strength
> J. WIlliford II can move 1 blood from an investment you control to your pool or from the blood bank to an investment as a +1 Stealth Action.
> Burn J. Williford II if you control no Investment Cards.
>
> Part of a series of cards which try to make investment cards a valid mechanic.
>
He's weak enough not to have a burn clause (and not feed the Khazar). And he could cost 0 pool considering that otherwise he will recoup his cost only two turns later after three actions spent.

Name: J. Williford II
Cardtype: Ally
Cost: 1 Pool
Unique mortal ally with 1 life. 0 strength, 0 bleed. Requires an investment card.
J. WIlliford II can move 1 blood from an investment card you control to your pool or from the blood bank to an investment card as a +1 stealth action.

But I'd rather have a non-unique "banker" so I can play more than 1 (investment being so crappy).

Name: Banker
Cardtype: Ally
Mortal ally with 1 life. 0 strength, 0 bleed. Requires an investment card.
Banker can move 1 blood from an investment card you control to your pool or from the blood bank to an investment card as a +1 stealth action.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: TheLich
Messages.Body: The original card was non unique but only targeted a single investment. I wanted to raise the power but was concerned about making it too powerful. The addition of the Requires an investment does fit better than the Burn clause. Thanks.
